title: Energy nudges: can data actually change behaviour?
excerpt: Early notes from my IVCCE research. The gap between what people say they'll do about energy and what they actually do is enormous.
html:
The project I'm working on at IVCCE is trying to answer a deceptively simple question: if you show people their energy usage in real time, will they change their behaviour?

Spoiler: kind of, but not in the way you'd expect.

What the literature says

There's a well-documented gap between intention and action in energy consumption. People say they want to save energy. They don't change their behaviour when shown abstract stats. But when you give them a specific, timely, contextual nudge — "your usage right now is 40% higher than usual" — something shifts.

The nudge has to be specific. It has to arrive at the right moment. And it has to propose an action, not just report a number.

What we're building

The smart nudging system we're designing tries to do exactly this — detect anomalous usage patterns and send targeted, actionable alerts at the moment they'll be most effective.

The ML component is the interesting part. Training a model on household usage data to distinguish between a normal Tuesday evening and one where something is obviously wrong.

Still early days. Will update as the research develops.
